conclusion.label: rejects

report:
Your skepticism is well-founded—the claim that "capsaicin treats breast cancer in humans" is not supported by current evidence.

**What the evidence shows:**

**Preclinical (lab/cell) studies are promising but not proof of human efficacy.** Numerous in vitro studies show capsaicin inhibits breast cancer cell lines (e.g., MDA-MB-231, MCF-7, BT-20) via mechanisms like G2/M cell cycle arrest, apoptosis, and modulation of EGFR/HER-2 pathways (nature.com/articles/onc2009335, dovepress.com "Capsaicin Inhibits Proliferation and Induces Apoptosis in Breast Cancer"). However, these are lab-dish findings, not evidence of a working human treatment.

**No clinical trials show capsaicin treats breast cancer itself.** The actual human trials found (CAPTRANE, QUCIP) test capsaicin patches only for *neuropathic pain after breast cancer surgery/chemotherapy*—not as a cancer treatment (mdpi.com/2072-6694/18/14/2355; pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11763653). A comprehensive review explicitly states "the clinical value of per os capsaicin to complement chemotherapy is still speculative" and calls the cancer literature "vast and controversial" (pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10177684).

**Key barriers:** Capsaicin has poor bioavailability, and its clinical development as an anticancer drug is limited by side effects like burning, stomach cramps, and nausea (frontiersin.org/journals/oncology/articles/10.3389/fonc.2022.908487/full).

**Epidemiology is mixed/concerning**, not supportive of a protective effect—some studies link heavy chili consumption to *increased* cancer risk (esophageal, gastrointestinal), complicating any "cancer treatment" narrative.

**Conclusion:** The claim is false as stated. Capsaicin shows anticancer activity only in cell/animal models; no human clinical trial demonstrates it treats breast cancer, and its only established clinical role in breast cancer patients is managing surgical/chemo-related nerve pain.

- https://www.nature.com/articles/onc2009335
- https://www.mdpi.com/2072-6694/18/14/2355
- https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/oncology/articles/10.3389/fonc.2022.908487/full
